And as Moses fasted 40 days and received the word of God written on the tablets and the Law, so also Christ, after His fast of 40 days, delivered His Gospel on earth and then His death on the cross, that is, He is the Word of God who redeemed us that we might live by Him.

Gifts for the tent, the ark, the table and the lampstand. God gave Moses on the mountain the details of setting up the tabernacle of the congregation, and it was so called because God meets in it with His people (Josh 19:51). It was also called the tabernacle of the testimony (Num 9:15) because in it are the tablets of the commandments that bear witness to God in the midst of His people, and because the tent testifies that God is the God of this people and lives among them. It was also called the dwelling place because God dwells in the midst of His people (2 Sam 7:6), and likewise it was called the house of the LORD (Judg 19:18) since worship of Him is offered in it. It was also called the temple (1 Sam 1:9) because God dwells in it. It consists of the dwelling, which includes the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, whose three walls are set up from wooden boards and covered with fabrics that become a roof for it and hang down on its sides and at its rear, while its door is made of a curtain, and a curtain also separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies. Inside the Holy of Holies is the ark of the covenant, which is the most important thing in the tent, and therefore He begins speaking of it in this chapter. And inside the Holy Place are three things: the table of the showbread, which is on the right of one entering the Holy Place, and in the middle the altar of incense, while on the left is the lampstand. Around the dwelling is the outer court, a courtyard surrounding the dwelling on all sides, and in front of the dwelling is the laver and before it the bronze altar.

The tent is surrounded by a fence made of wooden boards covered with curtains and fixed in the ground by bases and pegs. The door of the tent is on the eastern side and is a curtain hung on wooden boards, like the door of the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, and when you pass through it and enter the outer court you find the bronze altar, followed by the laver, then the door of the Holy Place, and after it the door of the Holy of Holies, which is on the western side. Entering the Holy of Holies is permitted only to the high priest, once a year, on the Day of Atonement, while the Holy Place is entered only by the priests every day, and the outer court surrounding the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, in which are the laver and the bronze altar, is permitted only to the Jews to enter, while non-Jews stand outside the tent.

The tabernacle of the congregation remained for 480 years. The first forty years were in the wilderness of Sinai, moving as God led the people by the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire (Ex 40:36-38); then in the land of Canaan Joshua set it up at Gilgal (Josh 4:19) and then moved it to Shiloh (Josh 18:1), where it remained for 400 years. King Saul moved it to Nob (1 Sam 21:1-9), and after that David moved it to Gibeon (1 Chr 21:9, 2 Chr 1:3), and it continued there until Solomon built the temple in its place on a larger scale and probably put its furnishings in one of the side chambers (1 Kgs 6:1). And the grief of the people was great when the enemies took the ark of the covenant of God in the days of Samuel the prophet, and they remained in weakness until God brought it back in the days of David (2 Sam 6:17), who rejoiced in it greatly, he and all the people.

God commanded Moses to collect gifts from the people for the founding of the tabernacle of the congregation, so that each one might show the extent of his care for the love of God, and their gifts would increase in proportion to their love for Him. And these gifts they offered from what they had taken from the Egyptians when they left the land of Egypt.

God specified the kinds of gifts required, and this is what everyone who manages a project must do, specify what is required for it. He began with the required metals, which carry symbolic spiritual meanings, and they are:
1- Gold: it signifies faith in God.
2- Silver: it signifies the word of God.
3- Bronze: it signifies endurance.
He continues the required materials, asking for kinds of fabrics and their requisites:
4- Blue: a light blue fabric that signifies heaven.
5- Purple: a fabric of a red color tending to violet, which is the garment of kings and signifies the kingship of Christ.
6- Scarlet: a dark red fabric that signifies the blood of Christ.
7- Goats' hair: used in making fabrics and tents, and it signifies death to the world.
8- Fine linen: that is, flax used in making fabrics and worn by the priests, and it signifies purity.
9- Rams' skins dyed red: used in covering the tent and dyed red, and it signifies death to the world.

10- Badgers' skins: the badger (tahash) is a sea animal with a thick skin, and it includes the seal, the dolphin and the sea horse, and it is used as an outer covering for the tent because its color and shape are not beautiful, and it signifies death to the world.
11- Shittim wood: strong wood that does not decay, used in making the firm foundation, and it signifies purity and endurance.

These are the coverings of the tent and its pillars, which are made of wood; they represent the outer protection, so they must be strong (see figure 1). Coverings of badgers' skins; coverings of rams' skins dyed red; coverings of goats' skins, west; coverings of white linen (fine linen), north; the tabernacle of the congregation; south; the outer court; east; the door, the only entrance of the tent. Figure (1:) The tabernacle of the congregation (Ex 25-30)
He adds materials that are consumed during the service in the tabernacle of the congregation, which are:
12- Oil: for lighting the lampstand, and it is pure olive oil, and it signifies the Holy Spirit.

13- Spices: sweet scents that are added and from which the anointing oil is made, and it will be mentioned in detail in (ch. 30:21-38); with it the priests and kings and the tent and its contents are anointed, and it signifies the Holy Spirit, who gives off a sweet fragrance.
He adds materials for adornment, which are:

14- Precious stones: onyx stones or various kinds with which the breastplate of the high priest is adorned, and they signify the dignity of the priesthood and the greatness of every soul in the sight of God, for each stone signifies a tribe.

The breastplate: the high priest wore it on his chest (ch. 28:15-30). Sanctuary: where God dwells in the midst of His people, and it is called the tabernacle of the congregation because in it God meets with His people.

The love of God moves Him to dwell in the midst of His people because He wants to be joined to them, and that they gather around Him always and be sanctified, and the tabernacle of the congregation is to be a place for the sanctification of the people and their purification from all evil. And Moses makes this tent according to the pattern that God will show him on the mountain, which will be mentioned now after these verses, for the Church is the image of heaven on earth.
Take care that God has a place inside you and that you return to Him in all your affairs through prayer, and offer Him the best of your time and abilities so that you may enjoy His work in you.

An ark: it is also called the ark of the covenant, since in it are placed the two tablets of the Law, which are God's covenant with His people, and it is also called the ark of the testimony, since God testifies to Himself by these commandments before His people. The ark is placed in the Holy of Holies.

He began with the ark of the covenant, which points to the presence of God, for it is the most important thing in the tent. It is made of firm shittim wood that does not decay, as a type of purity and immortality. He gives its measurements in cubits, a cubit being about 50 cm, so its length is one and a quarter meters and its width 75 cm and its height 75 cm (figures 1, 2). Figure (2:) The ark of the covenant

The ark is overlaid with gold inside and out. Gold signifies divinity and heaven, for the splendor of divinity is within it and without it, and therefore he took care that the ark be overlaid on the inside although no one would see it. The crown around the ark signifies glory, and the purpose of making it is adornment and also to hold the cover in its place.
Thou shalt cast: you melt the gold and pour it into molds so that it has the required shape.

He also makes for the ark four feet, that is, four supports on each side on which the ark stands, and he makes on them four rings of gold, two on each side, for the staves to pass through by which the ark will be carried.

He also makes two staves of firm shittim wood and overlays them with gold and puts them in the rings, one on one side of the ark and the other on the other side, and they remain in them always so that the Levites may carry the ark by them when it is moved from one place to another during their journeying in the wilderness, because the ark is always covered and no one touches it because of its holiness, so the Levites carry it by the two staves only, and therefore the staves are never taken out of the ark. The two staves signify the priesthood, through whose help we are joined to God.
They dispensed with them in the temple of Solomon since there was no need to move the ark from place to place.

The most important thing placed in the ark is the tablets of the Law, that is, the tablets of the covenant written on two tablets of stone, and with them will also be placed the pot of manna and Aaron's rod (Heb 9:4), and the rod signifies divine care and the priesthood.

The tablets of the testimony: because by them God testifies to His people the word by which they ought to live, and having lived by it they testify by their lives to the whole world that they are the people of God.
Let the word of God be inside your heart and nothing else, for it is what moves your life and changes your conduct, so that your heart is not occupied with the cares or material things of the world.

The cover is the lid of the ark and is made of pure gold, and it is called the mercy seat or the throne, and it signifies the mercy of God, since blood is sprinkled on it every year and divine justice, represented by the cherubim, sees it and pardons human beings; and this blood is a reference to the blood of Christ. It is the size of the ark, that is, its length is one and a quarter meters and its width 75 cm. It is placed on the ark and the crown surrounding the ark bounds it and encircles it on all sides, so that the cover does not move; the crown works as a barrier that keeps the cover in its place so that it does not fall from above the ark. The cover is made of pure gold because it signifies Christ, who covered us and made atonement for us by His blood, and it also signifies the Virgin, over whom the angels overshadow because Christ is in her womb.
Of beaten work: casting.

He asked him to make two angels of the rank of the cherubim, that is, the Cherubim, which signify divine justice. They are all made of gold, one piece with the cover, the head of each one facing the other and looking toward the cover, and each angel stretches his wings toward the other so that they meet at their tips. The form of the angel is probably the form of a man, and they look toward the cover, toward the blood that will be sprinkled upon it, so that when divine justice sees the blood, which points to the blood of Christ, that is, divine mercy, it pardons man. And the wings are raised on high to declare that they are from heaven.
And the cherubim are a great angelic rank that signifies abundant knowledge, since they are full of eyes, and they represent:
1- The presence of God.
2- Divine justice, when they were placed at the gate of the garden of Eden to prevent man's return (Gen 3:24).
3- The praise of God.

God declared that He would speak with His people from above the cover, because the ark signifies Christ, the wood His body and the gold His divinity. And God will speak from between the angels, which signify His justice, and at the same time from above the mercy seat on which the blood is sprinkled, so His justice will be mingled with His mercy when He speaks with the people.
And from the foregoing we see that the ark and the cover signify Christ in the following:
1- The presence of God in the midst of His people.
2- The wood signifies the humanity and the gold the divinity, so the ark signifies Christ, God incarnate.
3- The ark contains the tablets of the Law, that is, the word of God, and Christ is the Word of God.
4- The ark contains the pot of manna, and Christ is the manna come down from heaven to give Himself as food for His people, that is, His most holy Body and Blood.
5- The ark contains Aaron's rod that budded, which signifies the incarnate Christ, who gave us life from death.

6- And the cover on which the blood is sprinkled signifies Christ, who paid our debts with His blood before divine justice. And all these types, that is, the ark and what is in it and on it, also signify the Virgin Mary, as appears from the Sunday Theotokia.
Seize the opportunity of your life to enjoy God's mercy through your repentance and return to Him, and so escape the punishment of His justice.

This table is also made of firm shittim wood and is placed on the right as the priest enters the Holy Place; its length is two cubits, about one meter, its width one cubit, about 50 cm, and its height a cubit and a half, about 75 cm (figure 3). Figure (3:) The table of the showbread
It is also overlaid with gold, and a crown is made for it that surrounds it and keeps the bread from falling off it.

The border is a belt that ties the legs together and fixes them, and it is below the surface of the table for placing the vessels on it. This border has a crown, that is, a lip that holds the vessels on it so that they do not fall, and it is a handbreadth below the surface of the table, that is, a handbreadth wide, and this handbreadth is probably equal to the grasp of the hand, about 10 cm, and it extends outside it by a handbreadth also.

Four rings are made on the border, which is the outer perimeter of the table, and two staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold are made and put in the rings for carrying the table during the journeying in the wilderness, a reference to the sojourn of the world.

He mentions the vessels used for the service of the table, which are: The dishes: plates by which the bread is carried to the table. The spoons: small dishes in which incense is placed. The covers and bowls: in which wine is placed.
And all these utensils are made of pure gold.

12 loaves are placed, the number of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel, in two rows on the table, six loaves in each row, for a week, and then they are changed and others put in their place, and the old ones are eaten only by the priests, and they signify Christ our satisfaction and the special grace given to the priests. It is called the showbread because it is placed before the face of God, so there is a special blessing in it. Frankincense and salt were placed on it, and the frankincense signifies the priesthood of Christ and the salt the covenant He made with us by our redemption on the cross, that we might live for Him.
May you take care to be nourished by the word of God and that your heart be open before Him in much prayer, and so receive His blessing.

The lampstand consists of three parts: a base, a shaft and six branches, and it is made from one block of gold that is beaten until it takes the shape of this lampstand, because the Holy Spirit is one essence that is not divided. The lampstand is placed on the left as the priest enters the Holy Place, and it is the only source of light inside it (figure 4). Figure (4:) The golden lampstand
The lampstand has seven branches: the upright shaft and three branches from each side of the shaft. And the number seven signifies the Holy Spirit, who works in the seven sacraments of the Church.

On each branch is a cup like the cup of a flower, and under it a knop, that is, a knot or a pomegranate. And there is a cup at the top of the branch with a flower inside it, that is, like the green leaves that have within them and at their top the colored petals of the flower. There are three cups on the branch, each cup with a pomegranate under it, so the three cups are in succession, one at the first third, the second at the top of the second third and the third at the top of the branch, which is where the oil and the lamps are.

This ornament was made on every branch, pomegranates and cups and flowers, to declare that God is the source of life for His people. And this life appears in the flowers and fruits of plants, that is, the cups, the flowers and the pomegranates. And the number three signifies the Holy Trinity.

The middle shaft between the six branches has along its length four cups with their flowers: the first at the top of the first quarter, the second at the top of the middle, the third at the top of the three quarters and the fourth at the top of the shaft. And the number four signifies the four corners of the inhabited world, that is, the Holy Spirit is one of the three hypostases who enlightens the whole world with its four corners. For God in His three hypostases is the source of light and life for every person.

Under every two branches where they come out of the shaft is a knop, that is, a small pomegranate; that is, at the going out of the branches there are three pomegranates, and from each pomegranate two branches come out. Thus the work of lighting is blended with the life that the pomegranate signifies, because the pomegranate is the fruit of a living plant, for the Holy Spirit is the source of light and life for every person.

The lampstand is made, as we mentioned, from one block of pure gold, because the Holy Spirit is the source of purity for the whole world. And gold signifies divinity and heaven, the dwelling of God, who gives us the Holy Spirit.

He places the lamps at the edge of each cup, that is, the wicks face toward the middle shaft, so that their light is more concentrated; this is what he calls "give light over against it", that is, the manifold work of the Holy Spirit in the form of the seven sacraments has one purpose that is gathered in the salvation of man and his union with God.
The tongs: similar to the tongs known now, used for adjusting the wicks and putting them in or lifting them.
A talent: equal to 44 kg of gold.

The snuffdishes: vessels like an ashtray now, small dishes in which the new wicks or those that have been used are placed (figure 4). The whole lampstand and its utensils are made of pure gold, which signifies the purity of the work of the Holy Spirit, and are made of the same one block as we mentioned, whose amount is a talent.
All these details Moses saw on the mountain as God showed them to him.

God is the source of enlightenment and guidance in every aspect of your life through His many-sided work. So ask for His guidance and submit to Him even if it conflicts with your mind or your emotions.
The coverings of the tent and its pillars

The altar of incense is placed in the middle of the Holy Place, before the Holy of Holies. It is different from the bronze altar, which stands before the door of the tabernacle of meeting in the outer court. It is made of durable acacia wood that does not rot and is overlaid with plates of gold (v. 38). As we said concerning the Ark of the Covenant, the wood signifies the humanity of Christ and the gold His divinity; the wood also signifies the Virgin, while the gold signifies Christ who was born of her womb (Figure 18). Figure (18:) The altar of incense

The dimensions of the altar of incense are a cubit in length and a cubit in breadth, that is, square, and its height is two cubits. It has four horns, which are part of the corner post and not horns attached to it, to declare that the altar's strength comes from itself. It signifies the mighty Christ, who offered Himself up on the Cross as an atoning sacrifice for us, like the fragrance of incense with which God is pleased with man.

The top of the altar, all its sides and its horns are covered with gold, that is, the divinity was united with the humanity perfectly in Christ. A crown, that is, a raised border, is made for it around its upper surface, as a beautiful sight and to protect the incense and the coals from falling to the ground.

Two gold rings are made, joined and united to the altar on its two sides, so that a pole of acacia wood overlaid with gold may be put through each of them to carry it. The altar of incense is placed in the middle of the Holy Place before the veil that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies; on its right is the table of showbread and on its left the golden lampstand.
Aaron: all the priests are meant.
He dresses the lamps: he prepares them and makes them ready.
He lights the lamps: that is, he kindles them.

The priests place the incense every morning and every evening when they change the oil and replenish it in the lampstand so that it gives light morning and evening. In the same way, they offer a burnt offering on the bronze altar morning and evening. All these declare that Christ offers for us a complete and continual redemption that rises as a sweet fragrance before God, so that He is pleased with us. He is the light of the world, and He works always in the believers by His Holy Spirit, like the continual incense and the lampstand that shines always in the Holy Place.
He warns against three things concerning the altar of incense, which are:

1- Offering strange incense other than the composition that God told Moses about, which will be mentioned in this same chapter (v. 34). This is a declaration that Christ alone, whom the incense signifies, is the Redeemer.
2- No sacrifice or offering is to be offered on it, because these are offered on the bronze altar, whereas this altar is set apart for incense only.
3- No wine or oil is to be poured on it, as is done on the bronze altar.

For the same purpose, namely that this altar is set apart for incense, the rite here declares one aspect of the Cross, which is the incense that signifies Christ, who pleased the Father by the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross like the fragrance of incense.
Most holy to the Lord: it is set apart for the service of God and cannot be used for any other purpose.

Aaron puts the blood on it once every year on the Day of Atonement (Lev 16:18, 19) before he enters the Holy of Holies with the incense. This confirms that the incense is a symbol of Christ who was slain for us on the Cross. The blood is an atonement for the sins of the priest and the people, and so the blood is mingled with the incense on the altar of incense, because the two are symbols of the one sacrifice of Christ.

May you be like Christ, so that you are a sweet fragrance before God through your thoughts, your words and your deeds. Rather, be distinct from the rest of the world, as a child of God who has the fragrance of Christ, and do not resemble the people of the world in their faults.

God commanded that the people be numbered and that a ransom be paid for each one of the males. Every man twenty years old and above pays an amount of silver to redeem his soul, and this is for the following reasons:
1- A declaration of every person's need of the redemption of Christ, who is the Word of God and is signified by the silver.

2- Thanksgiving to God, who redeemed the firstborn of the children of Israel, and the destroying angel did not kill them in Egypt. This signifies responding to the love of Christ the Redeemer, who gave Himself on the Cross for His children, so we give Him our money, that is, the silver.

God warned against neglecting the numbering and the payment of the ransom, lest a plague come upon them as happened in the days of David. God's anger against David was because of his numbering of the people, for:
1- God had not commanded him to make this numbering.
2- David tried to boast of their number, that is, he fell into the sin of pride (2 Sam 24:10-17).

Twenty years old: the completion of maturity and the age of majority. Whoever reaches this age joins the army to fight (Num 1:3). The tribe of Levi was exempted from paying the ransom because they are consecrated to the service of the Lord (Num 1:

47-53.(Everyone who passes over to those who are numbered: that is, everyone who has reached the age of twenty and above and has passed under the counting. The shekel of the sanctuary: the priests kept accurate scales in the Temple, so it was called the shekel of the sanctuary, that is, a shekel that is exact and precise, more than the ordinary shekel, and it is about 12 grams of silver.
Gerah: that is, a grain, because it weighs a carob seed, and it equals 1/20 of the shekel of the sanctuary, that is, about 0.6 grams.

Every man offered half a shekel, that is, about 6 grams (some say 8 or 9 grams), which in any case is an amount of silver that both the poor and the rich can pay, since every soul has the same value before God, whether the person is rich or poor. It is a symbol of man's response to God's love and his appreciation of redemption. Christ paid the tax of the two drachmas, which is the ransom (Mt 17:24-27).

This silver is used in the building materials of the tabernacle of meeting, that is, for the bases of the pillars and the hooks. The silver signifies Christ the Redeemer, for redemption is the foundation of the spiritual building.

Remember the love of Christ the Redeemer and His care for you, so that you may respond to it, not only by giving the firstfruits and the tithes, but by serving God and laying down your life for His sake.

The laver is a wide vessel, most likely circular in shape, with a base on which it rests. It is made of bronze, which signifies steadfastness and strength, and water is put in it, and it is placed between the bronze altar and the Holy Place. It signifies Baptism, by which we are born again and are established in the life with God. It is circular because it signifies the salvation offered to the whole world, and no measurements were specified for it, so that it might declare salvation to everyone who believes in Christ (Figure 19). Figure (19:) The laver

The priests wash in this laver before they come forward to serve, as a declaration of the importance of purity before entering the service of God, and as a symbol of Baptism, the entrance to the spiritual life. The laver is placed between the bronze altar and the Holy Place, but washing in it is required before entering any service, whether at the bronze altar or in the Holy Place. It was placed before the Holy Place because those who wash in it are the priests only, who alone enter the Holy Place.
The washing of the hands is a sign of the purity of deeds, and the washing of the feet a sign of the purity of conduct.

Washing was necessary, otherwise the priest would die if he entered without washing, since this would be considered contempt for God's commands and His dwelling place. Washing is a symbol of the purity that Christ the Redeemer gives us.

Take care of the purity of your mind and its cleansing, and of casting all your troubles on God, before any spiritual work such as prayer at home, the Divine Liturgy, or reading the Holy Bible, by reading a psalm, making prostrations (metanoias), or repeating a hymn....
Calamus: a sweet fragrance.
Spices of fragrance: that is, a perfumed or sweetened perfume.
1- Pure myrrh (liquid myrrh): a gum that flows from one of the thorny trees and falls from it in drops, so it is called liquid myrrh, and it is the purest kind of myrrh since it has no impurities.
2- Sweet cinnamon: the inner bark of the cinnamon tree, which has a well-known sweet fragrance in addition to its pleasant taste.
3- Sweet calamus: a kind of reed that has a sweet fragrance.

4- Cassia: the bark of one of the trees, which has a sweet fragrance. Some say it is the outer bark of the cinnamon tree, though it may be another tree. It is called cassia (salikha) because the outer bark is stripped (tuslakh) from the trees.

God specified the quantities of these materials to be mixed together, with a hin of olive oil added to them, which is about 4 liters. These quantities come in the end to about 18 kilograms. Thus the anointing oil is formed with a sweet fragrance, and with it the kings, priests and prophets are anointed. It signifies the Sacrament of the Holy Myron.

He commanded him to anoint all the parts of the tabernacle of meeting, so that they would be dedicated, or sanctified, or consecrated to God, and a blessing to everyone who touches them, and not be used for anything except worship.
This anointing is used to anoint the priests, as has passed in (ch. 29).

This oil differs from all the perfumed oils that people use to give a fragrance to their bodies, and even if they use the same materials, they would be in different quantities. But whoever disobeys the word of God and makes the same exactly, to perfume his own body or the body of any person who is a stranger to the children of Israel, that person is set apart and cut off, that is, he does not become a member in the congregation of God.

May you have the virtues that adorn your life, and likewise holy worship and self-sacrificing service, so that your fragrance may be sweet before God, like the anointing oil, which is the work of the Holy Spirit.
The Lord gave Moses the ingredients of the composition of the incense, which are:-
1- Stacte: the gum of the storax tree.
2- Onycha: the shells of a water creature called the "winged-shell mollusk," which has a sweet fragrance when burned.
3- Galbanum: one of the fragrant gums.
4- Frankincense: a gum from thorny trees.
All these materials are mixed in equal quantities, and they give a sweet fragrance when burned.
These materials are mixed with salt and become holy incense, that is, set apart for the worship of God.
The preceding materials are beaten small, and they become the holy incense, which is placed in a golden vessel beside the altar of incense, before the Holy of Holies.

This incense, with the preceding quantities, is set apart for the worship of God, and no one may make the like of it to enjoy its fragrance in his house, out of honor and sanctification of this incense. Whoever makes the like of it is cut off from the people of God, that is, he is cast out and loses his membership.
The Church in the New Testament uses incense for the following reasons:
1- It was and still is offered as honor to God. God commanded it to Moses in the Old Testament, and its idea remains firm in the New Testament.
2- Offering feelings of love for God, like the sinful woman in the house of Simon (Lk 7:36-50) and like David in his prayers (Ps 141:2).
3- It signifies Christ the Redeemer, who offered His life for us on the Cross, and His good Father smelled a sweet fragrance on Golgotha.
4- It signifies the prayers of the saints and of all the believers, with which God rejoices, as the Book of Revelation declares (Rev 5:8, 8:3, 4).
5- Just as incense rises toward heaven as a sweet fragrance, so the life of the believers should rise with their virtues as a sweet fragrance toward heaven.

For your fragrance to be sweet before God, your life must be mixed with many virtues, and you must crush yourself with the sorrows of toil and spiritual striving, so that your heart and your life become holy to Christ.
The makers of the tabernacle of meeting and the sanctification of the Sabbath

entries.section: (1) The makers of the tabernacle of meeting

paragraphs.text: Bezaleel: his name means in the shadow or protection of God. He was the grandson of Hur, who supported the hand of Moses when he was praying at the time of the war with Amalek (ch. 17:10). Because of the greatness of the house of God, that is, the tabernacle of meeting, after He had specified to Moses everything in the tabernacle, its measurements and its design, He also supported it by choosing the one responsible for making the tabernacle. He chose a Jewish man named Bezaleel from the tribe of Judah, from which Christ, the leader of the journey of our salvation, came, and made him the chief of the craftsmen for the work of the house of God. The following is noted in his selection:
1- The most important arrangement for completing the service is the servant himself, so God took care in choosing Bezaleel to lead the work.

2- God chose him because he knew many crafts, which he had learned in Egypt, advanced in the arts at that time, and then filled him with understanding and knowledge by His Holy Spirit. Thus the grace of God is mingled with human knowledge, whose source is also God.

3- He knows many trades; he is an artist and is able to lead the craftsmen in the various crafts, even if some of them are more skilled than he in a particular craft, yet he is able to lead them. The leader organizes the work and leads it even if some of his followers are more gifted than he in a certain part of the work.

Care for the leader of every ministry and support him spiritually, emotionally and materially so that he may lead the work. Pray that God will send him, and be careful in your choice of him. And if you are a leader, take care for the purity of your heart and trust in God in everything, so that He may do His work.

entries.section: (1) The makers of the tabernacle of meeting

paragraphs.text: Aholiab: the meaning of his name is tent of the father. God chose him from the tribe of Dan, which is the least of the tribes in standing, because God loves everyone and chooses His servants from every place. Just as He chose Bezaleel from the tribe of Judah, from which Christ came, He chose Aholiab from a tribe of lesser rank.

To complete the service, God commanded Moses to appoint a helper for Bezaleel, namely Aholiab, and likewise to call all the artists in the various crafts to take part in this great work, to confirm the importance of cooperation and participation in work within the Church.

entries.section: (1) The makers of the tabernacle of meeting

paragraphs.text: He did not forget anything inside the tabernacle of meeting, whether the furniture or the materials used, for everything has value in the house of God and must be cared for because it is in the house of God.
At the end of God's talk with Moses on the mountain, He returns to confirm the importance of keeping the Sabbath. The following is noted in this commandment:
1- He calls them "My Sabbaths," for the people of God sanctify the seventh day for the sake of God, His worship and His love.

2- Keeping the day of God every week is a sign of our sonship to God. By this we differ from the rest of mankind, who do not care to set apart a day for God. It is like a covenant between God and His people throughout all the days.

3- He repeats it after the command to make the tabernacle of meeting, lest the workers think that it is permitted to work on erecting the tabernacle on the Sabbath days. It was required to devote oneself to worship only on this day.

If the glory of Sunday has surpassed the glory of the Sabbath because of the Resurrection of Christ, the Sabbath signifies rest not only in the completion of the creation of the world, but it signifies Sunday, on which Christ completed our redemption and proclaimed our salvation. Therefore may you take care to sanctify Sunday and give yourself a greater opportunity on it to enjoy the worship of God and His service, so that you experience His work in you more deeply.
Profanes it: breaks it.
God completes His commandments of the law of the Sabbath, saying:

4- The penalty for breaking the Sabbath by doing material works on it was severe, namely death, because the Sabbath signifies the devotion of the heart to God. Whoever lets the love of the world into his heart profanes it and has no life with Christ. This is the first time the penalty for breaking the Sabbath is mentioned, as it is mentioned in (Num 15:

God rested and was refreshed: what is meant is God's satisfaction with His work, for God does not grow weary or breathe as human beings do, but He speaks in expressions that human beings understand, to teach them that rest is a spiritual rest, by being with God.
God adds in the law of the Sabbath:

5- The necessity of holding fast to it throughout their lives and in all generations, that is, their children. Even now the Sabbath day has respect in the Church, but the glory of Sunday has surpassed it, so the Church celebrates Sunday and also the Sabbath of every week, and does not fast strictly on them nor make prostrations (metanoias), because they are days of joy. Here He stresses the importance of continuing to keep the Sabbath, that is, carrying out God's commandments throughout life.

entries.section: (1) The making of the golden calf

paragraphs.text: Moses represented the image of God to the people. So when he went up the mountain and was absent there for days, they needed a tangible image, as they had seen images of gods in Egypt. They asked Aaron for a tangible image of God to worship in place of Moses, because they doubted whether he might have died on the mountain, since he had no food or drink for the whole forty days (ch. 25:18), or whether he had lost his way in the mountain, or the divine fire had burned him. Some of them may have thought that he had been caught up to heaven like Enoch. Moses spent another forty days fasting on the mountain (ch. 34:28) to receive two new tablets of the commandments, after he broke the first two tablets when he came down from the mountain and saw the golden calf (v. 19).

entries.section: (1) The making of the golden calf

paragraphs.text: Fashioned it: melted it so that it became a single mass.

Aaron yielded to the people's sinful demands. This was weakness of faith and fear on his part before the people's uprising. So he collected from them the golden earrings that were in their ears, melted them in the fire, and fashioned them with a graving tool, and he formed a calf from this gold and called it the god who brought the children of Israel out of Egypt by the ten plagues. This was a belittling of God by depicting Him as a calf, as they used to worship the calf "Apis" in Egypt or watch the Egyptians worship it. Notice the generosity of the people in giving to make the golden calf, just as we give much of our time and effort to evil. Notice also that the Holy Bible mentions the sins of the saints just as it mentions their virtues, so that we are not troubled if we fall into sin, but rise and continue our spiritual striving with God.

Hold fast to the word of God as a servant, and do not yield to the demands of those you serve in order to please them against the commandments of God, so that your only aim in every service is to draw souls to Christ.

entries.section: (1) The making of the golden calf

paragraphs.text: After Aaron set up the golden calf, raised before the people, he built an altar before it and offered sacrifices on it, and they ate of them. It appears that peace offerings, part of which is burned before God on the altar while the one who offers them eats the remainder, were known among the fathers since the days of Adam. By this Aaron proclaimed a feast to the Lord Jehovah, depicted in the form of this golden calf. By making the golden calf and what they did before it, they fell into these errors:
(1) Belittling God and depicting Him as a golden calf.
(2) Offering sacrifices to this idol, which neither hears nor sees nor walks.
(3) They were absorbed in eating meat, rather than in repentance joined with offering sacrifices to God.
(4) They took part in licentious and shameless games to please their lusts, and most likely these were joined with drinking wine.

At the end of the forty days, after God finished His talk with Moses, He informed him of the evil into which the people had fallen, and commanded him to go down from the mountain to the people, who had become corrupt by making a golden calf. They offered it worship and sacrifices, and even attributed to it the power of bringing them out of the land of Egypt, and they departed far from their God. In God's distress over the people, He called them "your people," for they were no longer the people of God, because they had exchanged Him for a golden calf.

Do not lose the grace of your sonship to God, in which you enjoy a relationship of love with Him and His care, and even the eternal inheritance. Do not give up all this for any earthly lust, however pleasant or dazzling it may seem, for it is passing away and is worth nothing beside your sonship to God.

Stiff-necked: like the ox that refuses to have the yoke placed on its neck, or the horse that resists with its neck the bridle placed in its mouth. What is meant is that the people of God are obstinate like these animals. God described His people as obstinate and as refusing life with Him, and He declared to Moses that He intended to destroy this people for their wickedness and to raise up a new people from his offspring, because he had found grace in His eyes, like Noah and Abraham. We notice Moses' boldness with God, so that he even asks His permission and He says to him, "Let Me alone." For God loves His children, and they have a great place with Him. He of course knows that Moses will intercede for the people and that He will not destroy them, but He declares how wicked they are and how much they deserve, without destroying them.
Repented of the evil: ceased from taking vengeance on them.
Moses raised his prayers in humility before God, pleading for His mercies, that He would forgive His people and not destroy them, for the following reasons:

1- Because they are the people of God, who kept them in Egypt and brought them out with great power and cares for them in the wilderness. They are His own and His children, and by this he seeks the tenderness and fatherhood of God.

2- That He not give the Gentiles, such as the Egyptians, an opportunity to speak arrogantly against God and claim that He hates His people and brought them out with cunning in order to destroy them in the wilderness, whereas God is tender and compassionate and does not lie in His promises. That is, that He not give them an opportunity to gloat over His people.

3- He reminds God of His promises to the fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, to give them the land of Canaan. Here the unselfishness of Moses appears: he does not think of himself and his house becoming the beginning of the people of God as Abraham did, but with fatherly love he cares for the salvation of all the people, even though they are wicked. Moses reminds God that the people are His people, so that He may have mercy on them.

The Lord repented: He turned back from His decision. It does not mean that He felt He had made a mistake, because God knows everything and does not err, but He speaks in the manner that human beings understand, namely that He is a tender Father who gave up His decision to destroy the people, agreed to Moses' intercession for his people, and abandoned His decision to destroy them. He knows what will happen and that Moses will intercede for them, but He wanted to declare what they deserve, and then, for the sake of Moses' intercession, to have mercy on them.

entries.section: (3) The anger of Moses and the breaking of the tablets

paragraphs.text: On both their sides: on both faces.

Moses obeyed and went down from the mountain, departing from the presence of God, whom he saw in a certain form that may have been light or some other dazzling and wonderful form. In his hands were the two tablets of stone that God had given him, with the Ten Commandments written on both sides of each tablet. The two tablets were made by God and written by Him, and Moses alone carried them in his hands, rejoicing in their great value.

entries.section: (3) The anger of Moses and the breaking of the tablets

paragraphs.text: After Moses had descended some distance on the mountain, he met his disciple Joshua, who had been waiting for him for the forty days. He rejoiced at meeting him, and they went down together. When they drew near the foot of the mountain, before they saw the people, they heard the sound of their shouting, and Joshua thought it was the sound of battle, perhaps the people fighting the Amalekites, who had risen against them a second time.

entries.section: (3) The anger of Moses and the breaking of the tablets

paragraphs.text: Being overcome: defeat.
Moses answered Joshua, denying his words and declaring that these sounds were not the sounds of battle, whether the voice of the victors or of the defeated, but the sound of the people singing.

entries.section: (3) The anger of Moses and the breaking of the tablets

paragraphs.text: Moses and Joshua continued descending from the mountain and drew near to the people, and Moses saw the golden calf raised up and the people around it dancing and singing. He became very angry at the corruption of his people in leaving God and worshiping idols, and in the intensity of his anger he cast the two tablets from him despite their great value. But he was jealous with the jealousy of a father who cares for his children when he saw them in this corruption and turning away from God.

entries.section: (3) The anger of Moses and the breaking of the tablets

paragraphs.text: When the people saw Moses coming quickly toward them, they were very afraid. He took the calf and threw it into the fire until it melted and became a shapeless mass, then he broke it and ground it into tiny particles and cast them into the water, and the particles floated on the surface of the water. He commanded the people to drink of it, to show them the weakness of what they had imagined to be a god, so that they would feel their sin against God when they drank, that perhaps they might repent.

Be firm with those who err, if you are responsible for your household or your work or a group of those you serve in the Church. Reject evil and remove it from the midst, keep those you serve away from it, and make them know the extent of their sin so that they may repent. But your firmness should be with fatherhood and embrace toward those you rebuke, so that they do not fall into despair or obstinacy.
Moses rebuked Aaron for yielding to the evil thoughts of the people by making a calf and calling them to worship it. By this he made them idolaters, and they disobeyed God and defied Him.
Aaron did not admit his fault but gave justifications for what he had done, which are:
(1) That the people fall into many evils, such as murmuring, as Moses knows.
(2) Moses represented the image of God to the people, so when he was absent on the mountain for a long time, they asked for a tangible image to worship.

(3) He lessened his sin by saying that he was compelled to ask them for the gold earrings and throw them into the fire, and so a calf came out, although in truth he had made an effort and used the graving tool and instruments to make a calf of gold; it did not become a calf by itself.

We notice that Aaron called Moses "my lord" although he was younger than he, out of respect for him because he was the leader of the people and the prophet of God. This speech shows the seriousness of the leader's sin, which brings punishment upon all his people, for Aaron's laxity and his yielding to the evil of his people made the people fall into the sin of idolatry.

Moses grieved when he saw a large number of the people stripped of their clothes, even if partially, and immersed in the shamelessness or licentiousness and dancing that Aaron had allowed as leader of the people, so they became a derision among their neighbors, such as the Amalekites.

Bear your responsibility, whether you are a servant, or the head of a family, or someone responsible in any place, to lead others in the way of God, and do not abandon them or encourage them in evil. For God will hold you accountable because you used your leadership and your position to keep people away from God.
The gate of the camp: the entrance to the place where they pitched their tents; perhaps they posted guards at it against an attack by the Amalekites or any of their enemies.
Who is on the Lord's side: whoever believes in God and fears Him and rejects evil.
Let him come to me: let him come toward me to help me destroy evil.

Moses stood in a visible place, which was the entrance of the place where they were dwelling, and called to the people that everyone who fears God and is zealous to please Him should gather around him. A large number of the men of the tribe of Levi, who cared for their spiritual life and their relationship with God, gathered with him.

When Moses declared the wrath of God over their worship of the calf, and had ground it, scattered it on the water and made them drink of it, many were ashamed and repented and went into their tents, but some neglected the words of Moses and persisted in their evil. Then he commanded the sons of Levi gathered around him that each one take his sword, which was placed in a sheath at the middle of each man and hung on his thigh, and pass through the tents and kill their brothers who persisted in the games of shamelessness and dancing and had stripped off their clothes. The sons of Levi obeyed the word of Moses at once and killed three thousand men of the wicked.
Consecrate yourselves (literally, fill your hands): sanctify and set apart your works for God.
Every man on his son and on his brother: by killing the wicked son or brother.

After the destruction of the evil, Moses encouraged them, saying that by this they had obeyed God and sanctified their works by destroying the wicked, even if they were their sons or their brothers, for their relationship with God is more important than emotional relationships, and by this God gives them a great blessing. Filling the hand was an expression used in the priestly work when they carry the sacrifices on their hands and offer them on the altar before God. So he called the tribe of Levi, which would be set apart for the service of God, and from which would come Aaron and his sons, to destroy the wicked, because by destroying evil they would be doing work like the priests who sanctify God, whether by offering sacrifices or by the various purifications. Here, by their destroying evil, they declare the holiness of God, who is not in agreement with evil, and please Him, and by destroying the wicked they also save the people from the spread of evil among them, so that the fear of God falls on all hearts.

On the day after the killing of the wicked, Moses showed his people how monstrous their sin was and that they deserved severe punishment, but he gave them hope that he would go up to the mountain and pray to God to ask forgiveness for their sin. This shows that many had sinned and bowed down to the calf, but they repented at Moses' call and went into their tents, and the Levites did not kill them.

Moses confessed the sin of his people before God when he returned and went up to the mountain, where he had been with God forty days. Then he interceded for them that God might forgive them, and offered himself as a ransom for his people, that he should die but the people live. Here the fatherhood of Moses appears and his readiness to lay down his life for his people as a good shepherd to them, after the pattern of Christ the Redeemer. The blotting out of his name from the book of God means his death, or not being mentioned in the Holy Bible as one of the pious. Moses was not able to redeem his people, because only Christ is able to die for His people and make atonement for them, but by these words he shows his intense love and fatherhood for his wicked people.

Pray for those around you and care for the salvation of their souls. Rather, be ready to sacrifice anything material and to bear many hardships in order to win them for Christ, remembering your Redeemer who laid down His life for you.

God rejoiced in the fatherly feelings of Moses for his people, but He showed His justice by declaring that the one who sinned is the one who bears the punishment, and if he repents God accepts him. It is not right that one person die for another, because of man's weakness and because Christ alone is able to do this in the fullness of time.
Lead the people: exhort them so that they do not return to evil and so that they repent of their sin.
The day of My visitation: the day that God appoints to punish and discipline His people so that they feel the monstrousness of their sins and keep away from them.

God asked Moses to go down from the mountain and exhort the people to an upright life. He promised him that His angel would not leave them because of their sin, but would continue to lead them in the form of the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire by day and by night, but that He would discipline them at the proper time so that they would not return to their sins. This means God's anger against them, so He deprived them of His presence in their midst and was content with the angel going before them.

God disciplined the people with plagues so that they would feel the monstrousness of idolatry. The kind of plagues is not mentioned, whether they were diseases or hunger or any other afflictions that God allowed for them, but what is mentioned is the death of three thousand of them in one day by the hand of their brothers (v. 28). Notice that His acceptance of Moses' intercession does not mean the complete removal of punishment from them but its lessening, whereas the complete removal of punishment is what is accomplished by the blood of Christ. This confirms the seriousness of sin and its consequences, which deserve many punishments, and so the love of Christ appears, which removes from us all these punishments.
God's leading of His people

Although the people of God fell into the worship of idols and departed from God, He did not reject them but remained faithful to His promises despite their unfaithfulness. So He spoke to Moses that he might prepare to enter the Promised Land, as God had promised the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

Be steadfast in your love for those around you, even if they wrong you or do not respond to your love... Make excuses for them, and know that the continuance of your love and care for them establishes you in love and gradually affects them, and qualifies you to receive many divine blessings, the first of which is that you enjoy a strong experience of the love of God and His work in your life.
God promised to bring them into the Promised Land, but their leader would be an angel whom God would send, and not God Himself, because of His anger against them on account of their worship of idols.

Flowing with milk and honey: an expression for the many good things they will find in the Promised Land. The reason God would not lead them Himself on their way to the Promised Land, which is full of good things, is that they are quick to disobey and rebel, so they deserve the wrath of God and are exposed to destruction, that is, God would destroy them as a punishment for them.

The people felt their sin when they heard from Moses that God refused to lead them, and they wept in repentance before God, declaring their sin and asking forgiveness from Him. They stripped off their ornaments as a declaration of their clinging to God and their rejection of anything material for His sake.
Horeb: the place where they made the golden calf.

God affirmed the obstinacy of the people, signified by the stiffness of the neck, as animals are stubborn and turn and twist their necks, refusing to bear the yoke, that is, the wood that is placed on their necks to pull the agricultural implements. Therefore God withdrew from leading them Himself, yet in His tenderness He gave them an opportunity to repent by saying, "put off your ornaments," that is, repent and humble yourselves before Me, and I will consider what to do with you. So they hastened to repentance, humility and prayer, and put off their ornaments. Putting off ornaments was a well-known practice used in the East as a sign of mourning.

(2) God speaks in the tabernacle (v. 7: 11:) 7 And Moses took the tabernacle, and pitched it without the camp, afar off from the camp, and called it the Tabernacle of the congregation. And it came to pass, that every one which sought the LORD went out unto the tabernacle of the congregation, which was without the camp. 8 And it came to pass, when Moses went out unto the tabernacle, that all the people rose up, and stood every man at his tent door, and looked after Moses, until he was gone into the tabernacle. 9 And it came to pass, as Moses entered into the tabernacle, the cloudy pillar descended, and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and the LORD talked with Moses. 10 And all the people saw the cloudy pillar stand at the tabernacle door: and all the people rose up and worshipped, every man in his tent door. 11 And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. And he turned again into the camp: but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle.

Moses had a tent in which he met with the elders of Israel and judged the people, and this was different from the tent in which he lived with his family. He moved this tent outside the camp, that is, the place where the children of Israel pitched their tents, as a declaration of God's wrath, which was still upon His people, until they completed their repentance. Everyone of the people who had a request before God would go out to this tent and ask Moses to pray for him and would seek God in this place. This shows the mercy of God, who did not forsake them completely but only showed His displeasure with them so that they would repent.

This tent is a symbol of the Church, because in it God meets with His people, so it was called the tabernacle of meeting. It is a prelude to the tabernacle of meeting and of the testimony, in which is the Ark of the Covenant, the pattern of which Moses saw on the mountain because it had not yet been made (chs. 25-27).

Every need you feel, present it to God in the Church, place it on the altar. For when God sees your faith and your clinging to Him and your hastening to Him, and not to reason, the world and people, He has compassion on you, solves all your problems and blesses your life.

When Moses went out from his tent, in which he lived with his family, and passed through the tents of Israel on his way to the tabernacle of meeting outside the camp, everyone would come out of his tent and stand in respect for him and ask for prayer for himself and his family, and they would remain standing in reverence until he reached the tabernacle of meeting and entered it to meet with God.

God would declare His presence and His being with Moses, when he entered the tabernacle of meeting, by the pillar of cloud descending, covering, and standing before the door of the tabernacle until God's talk with Moses was finished. Moses would hear Him clearly and speak with Him, and then report to the people God's commands and commandments. Therefore he was called the one to whom God spoke, because of the abundance of His speaking with him. Because of his righteousness he reached the degree of direct conversation with God. By this he was able to lead the people with God's guidance, so that every servant and every head of a family may learn that prayer is the foundation of his success in leading those he serves and cares for.
When the people saw God appearing in the pillar of cloud, they would fear and bow down at once, each one before the door of his tent, in reverence and humility, asking for the mercies of God.

A wonderful friendship of the highest level was enjoyed by Moses with God through his successive meetings with Him in the tabernacle. His servant and disciple Joshua the son of Nun accompanied him and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and when Moses finished speaking with God and went to the people to teach them, Joshua would remain in the tabernacle in continual prayers and worship. Thus we see how God prepared Joshua through his discipleship to Moses and his learning worship for long periods, as he left his family and stayed in the tabernacle until the tabernacle of the testimony was made, in which is the Ark, and the Levites became responsible for guarding it and being present in it. Notice that this temporary tent was outside the camp as a declaration of God's wrath, but after they offered repentance, Moses set up the permanent tabernacle of meeting in the midst of the camp.

entries.section: (3) Moses' intercession that God might lead His people

paragraphs.text: Moses appealed to God and said to Him, You commanded me to bring up this people and take them to the land of Canaan, and You did not tell me whom You will send with me, meaning that You refused to lead the people Yourself, as You Yourself brought us out of the land of Egypt into the wilderness. He pleaded with Him to lead them and bear with them and not send with them only an angel, and he based his appeal on the following:
(1) God said, You have declared that You know me by name, that is, that You have loved me.

(2) In humility Moses declared his ignorance in leading the people and his need of God to make the way known to him. (3) Moses showed his longing to know God, as though he did not yet know Him, although he had a long fellowship with Him; he is ambitious to know God every day more than before.
(4) He reminds God that the children of Israel are His own people, for whom He is responsible, for He is their Father, their Shepherd and their God.

God is very tender, so ask of Him all that you want, and whatever your sins may be, know that He is ready to forgive you, and even if He is angry with you, continue in your supplication and humility before Him until you obtain His mercies.

entries.section: (3) Moses' intercession that God might lead His people

paragraphs.text: God agreed, before the appeal of Moses, to go Himself in the midst of His people and lead them. Moses affirmed that he would not move with this people except under the leadership of God, for remaining in the wilderness with God is better than entering the Promised Land with all its good things without God, because he loved God above all the material things of the world and found in Him his rest and reassurance.

entries.section: (3) Moses' intercession that God might lead His people

paragraphs.text: Moses continues his talk with God, declaring that the reason for his distinction and that of his people from all the peoples of the earth is the presence of God in their midst. He is the most precious thing in his life and the life of his people, and by this this people declare their faith in God to the whole world, so that they may believe and join the people of God and find their salvation. In the face of Moses' love and clinging to God, God affirmed to him that He would go before him and would not leave them, because He loved Moses and found in him righteousness and holiness.
Moses made a wonderful request that no one had made before, namely to see God. Although he had spoken with Him much, his longing for God led him to make this request.
I will make all My goodness pass before you: I will present My mercies before you, and My blessings and My good things.

I will proclaim the name of the LORD before you: I will declare Myself before you so that you may believe in Me and live with Me, you and your people. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy: I give My love to whom I choose, and he is the one who believes in Me and responds to Me, and I pour out mercies upon him.

God said to him, I will give you many blessings and declare My name before you and have mercy on you, so you will see Me through these blessings and declarations and mercies, and this is quite enough.

God said to Moses, I love you and you have found grace in My sight, but this request of yours is beyond your endurance, for no man can see Me, meaning the seeing of the essence of God, because he would die from the greatness of the light of God and His brightness, which exceeds the capacities of human beings. For the angels, who are great creatures, cannot look at God but hide their faces from the brightness of His glory (Isa 6:2).

The tenderness of God could not bear, before the request of Moses and his insistence, to deprive His son of seeing Him, so He let him see Him to the extent that he could bear. God took Moses upon a rock and put him in a cleft and covered him with His hand, and then God passed by in His glory, that is, a great dazzling light appeared. Then God lifted His hand, and Moses saw something of the brightness of God, which is what he could bear as a man. He rejoiced greatly, and indeed his face was clothed with intense radiance, so that the children of Israel afterward could not bear to look at him and asked him to put a veil over his face (ch. 34:34, 35). Moses' seeing of God signifies the Incarnation of Christ. When God said, "Behold, there is a place by me," He meant the fullness of time when Christ became incarnate in Bethlehem, and the rock signifies Christ, upon whom the believer stands and sees God, and He reveals to him as much as he can bear. This is what we behold in the New Testament at Communion from the Holy Mysteries, and as God reveals Himself to His saints in the wildernesses throughout the ages. All this we behold now on earth, but in heaven we shall be able to see Him more clearly. Here we see Him as in a mirror, but there face to face, where our earthly bodies are changed and become spiritual bodies able to enjoy the sight of God clearly (1 Cor 13:10-12).

God loves you and wants to reveal His secrets to you if you want Him and seek Him. This appears in your striving toward prayer, reading and meditation, for in proportion to your care God will let you experience Him and rejoice in Him. The renewal of the covenant

God asked Moses to cut two tablets so that God might write on them the Ten Commandments. So he cut the two tablets in a reasonable size that could be carried and also afterward placed in the Ark of the Covenant. Notice that the two tablets the first time were made by the hand of God, but the second time Moses made them, so that God might show them the result of their sin in worshiping the golden calf, which angered Moses so that he broke the tablets.
Do not be careless in seizing every spiritual opportunity to draw near to God and to thank Him for His gifts, lest these blessings be lost to you and you not find them even if you seek them much.

He commanded him to rise early in the morning and go up with the tablets on the mountain to its top, that is, its head, which is most likely the same place where God appeared to him the first time and gave him the commandments.

He also commanded him that no man go up with him, as the first time, such as Aaron and Joshua, because God would appear to him more and give him more blessings, such as the radiance of his face. He also commanded that no one come near the mountain, not even the animals, so that all might feel its awe and holiness. Moses carried out the word of God and went up with the tablets on the mountain.

He stood with him there: Moses stood in the cleft in which God had put him (ch. 33:22). After Moses went up to the top of the mountain, God appeared to him in the form of a great cloud, and then he heard a voice from heaven proclaiming that God had come. This stirs feelings of awe and fear and at the same time longing and love within Moses.

God moved before him in the form of a great cloud, which may have been accompanied by a strong light, and then he heard a voice calling the name of the LORD, and the repetition of this was a confirmation of the presence of God Himself, and declaring the attributes of God, which are: (1) Mercy and tenderness toward His people, and pity and compassion for them.
(2) Longsuffering, for He does not become angry with His people quickly if they err and gives them an opportunity to repent. (3) His gifts are many and never end.
(4) He fulfills His promises.
He will by no means clear the guilty: He will not forgive those who persist in sin, whether fathers or children. The voice continues the attributes of God, saying:
(5) God gives His blessings to His people however large their number, whether in the same generation or in the following generations.
(6) God is forgiving to all who repent, whatever their sins.
(7) God is just, so He does not forgive the one who does not repent and persists in sin, and He punishes the children and grandchildren if they walk in the sins of their fathers.

Enjoy the mercies of God, for He is tender beyond all imagination, and seize every opportunity for repentance, and do not be lax with any sin however small, and do not justify it, because He is also just.
If now I have found grace in Your sight: since I have found grace in Your sight.
Moses felt the fear of God and the greatness of His love, so he showed his submission to Him by bowing down on behalf of himself and all his people, and asked of God:

(1) That He go in the midst of His people and bear with their obstinacy and disobedience and give them an opportunity to repent. (2) That He forgive the sins of his people because they felt their sin.
(3) That He have compassion on His people and accept to be King over them.

When God found Moses' response, He promised him not only forgiveness and mercy but the doing of great and awesome wonders, such as their crossing the Jordan River and victory over the peoples dwelling in the land of Canaan. Thus God renewed His covenant with His people.
God declared His covenant with His people with His many blessings mentioned in His previous attributes, and as for the people, their undertaking appears in the following:
(1) Not making a treaty with the wicked inhabitants of the land in Canaan, lest the children of God mingle with them and be defiled by their evil. This happened, sadly, in the days of the Judges.
Their pillars (sacred stones): stone pillars set up for the pagan gods.
Their wooden images (Asherim): wooden poles set up on the high places for the gods of the sky, such as the stars.

(2) Tearing down the altars and the pillars and cutting down the wooden images, as a rejection of pagan worship, because the children of Israel worship God, and He is jealous over them like a bridegroom over his bride, and He is very angry if they mix His worship with their worship of idols.

(3) Not making a treaty with the wicked, lest they mingle with them and flatter them and so take part in the worship of their idols and eat what is sacrificed to them, and by this commit spiritual adultery by leaving the worship of God and turning to the worship of idols.
(4) Not letting their sons marry pagan women, lest they draw them into the worship of idols and so they fall into spiritual adultery.
(5) He warned them against imitating the pagans in making images and worshiping them.

(6) He stressed to him some positive laws that He had mentioned to him the previous time when He gave him the two tablets, so He reminded him to keep the feast of the Passover and the days of Unleavened Bread that follow it, seven days, that is, the feast of Unleavened Bread at the beginning of the seven days and at their end, as was mentioned before (ch. 12), in sanctification of their coming out of the land of Egypt in the month of Abib.

(7) He also reminded him of the law of redemption, because God killed the firstborn of Egypt and redeemed the firstborn of His people. So every firstborn is offered to God, and likewise the firstborn of the animals, except the donkey, which is redeemed with a lamb (ch. 13). Thus he does not appear before God empty-handed but offers his gifts to God. This was explained before in (ch. 23).
(8) He reminded him to keep the law of the Sabbath, which is the fourth commandment, even if it be in the season of plowing or harvest (ch. 20:4).
(9) He also alerted him to the feasts of Weeks and Ingathering (ch. 23).

(10) He commanded him to keep the three feasts, that is, the Passover, Weeks (Pentecost) and Ingathering (Tabernacles), at which all the males come to celebrate before God. He promised him, if he keeps the commandments of God, the following: (a) The driving out of the pagans, the inhabitants of the land.

(b) He will bless his land and grant him to possess the Promised Land. The borders of the kingdom of the children of Israel were greatly enlarged in the days of Solomon (1 Kgs 4:21), but they shrank when they fell into many sins, and indeed the enemies occupied it completely during the captivity.
(c) None of the pagans will covet or dare to enter his land when his males go up to celebrate the three feasts of God.
(11) He warns him against using leaven at the feast of the Passover or leaving any of its meat until the next day, as was mentioned before in (ch. 12).
(12) He commanded him to bring the firstfruits of his produce to God (ch. 23). (13) He commanded him not to boil a young kid that is still nursing (ch. 23).
If you want to enjoy the mercies of God, you must keep His commandments with all care, and if you err, repent quickly, and then He fulfills all His covenants to you.

God asked Moses to write the laws that He had told him in a book, so that he might teach them to the people and they might not forget them, and might be committed to them, and so keep the covenant of God and receive His blessings.

Moses spent forty days and forty nights with God fasting; he neither ate nor drank during them, and this was by divine help and power. This is the second time of Moses' fasting forty days and forty nights; the first was when he received the two tablets the first time (ch. 24:18), and Elijah fasted the like (1 Kgs 19:18), and then Christ (Mt 4:2). This fast is a miracle that exceeds the capacities of human beings and was accomplished by the power of God. Moses spent this period praying for Aaron and all the people, and God may have stressed to him some commandments and laws that were mentioned before (chs. 21-24), and the design of the tabernacle and its erection (chs. 25-31), and at its end God commanded him to write the Ten Commandments on the two tablets that Moses had made. Notice here that the two tablets the second time were made by Moses and not by God, as a discipline for him because he became angry and in the heat of his anger broke the first two tablets, which God Himself had made. Then God wrote the Ten Commandments on the two tablets with His finger.
Do not fear the difficulty of the commandment or of the spiritual practices of prayers and fasts, because God will give you help to fulfill them and to enjoy in them fellowship with God.

After Moses received the two tablets of the law the second time from God, He gave him a grace, which was that his face shone with a great radiance as a declaration of his righteousness and holiness, so that the people would submit to him and obey the words of God on his tongue. So God adorns His children in every generation with virtues that they do not see, because of their humility, but people notice in them very clearly.

God is ready to give you a special grace so that others may revere and respect you, and you may show them the word of God. Therefore be careful in your speech and remember that you are the voice of God to those around you, so let no evil word come out of your mouth.

Moses came down from the mountain and went to meet the people under the leadership of Aaron, and they were this time waiting for him with care, and were surprised by the radiance of his face and feared greatly and felt the fear of God when he approached them, which made them keep further and further from their sins.

Moses approached Aaron and the leaders of the people, who were in great fear of the radiance of his face, and he spoke to them all that God had commanded him. Then he approached the people, who also feared the brightness of his face, and perhaps they looked at the ground in humility because they could not bear to see the radiance of his face, and he also told them of the commands of God.

Moses did not know that his face was shining, but the people told him of it, and indeed declared that they could not bear to see the radiance of his face and asked him to cover it. So out of pity for them he put a veil or covering on his face when he approached them and taught them. And when he left them and entered the tabernacle of meeting to speak with God, he would remove the veil from his face.

There is another opinion in the interpretation of this part, that Moses, besides removing the veil in his talk with God in the tabernacle, would keep the veil removed when teaching the people so that they might feel the fear of God, and then put it back on his face in his ordinary talk with the people.
St. Paul the Apostle spoke of this veil in (2 Cor 3:7-18) to show that the knowledge of God was still obscure in the Law, but in the New Testament it appeared clearly.

The veil signifies your weakness and your inability to see the works of God and His glory. The more you live a life of repentance, the more you can hear the voice of God and see His works in all the events around you, and you can understand His word in the Holy Bible. Ask for His help in humility, and He will remove from you every barrier that hinders you from sensing Him and understanding Him.
